pr_title: Support SmartStrip type devices (HS300, HS107) in tplink component
pr_body:
Add support for SmartStrip type devices (HS300, HS107) to tplink component

## Description:

This adds a new `strip` type to the tplink component as well as detects strip type devices during discovery and uses a pyHS100 SmartStrip to iterate the SmartPlug(s) and adds each of them as a switch to HA. This also fixes state reporting for multi-plug devices and reports the state of each plug correctly.

**Related issue (if applicable):** fixes #25146

**Pull request with documentation for [home-assistant.io](https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io) (if applicable):** home-assistant/home-assistant.io#10914

hands and restarting the server (or trying the underlying library, but
that's even more complex).

issue_context.title: Kasa HS300 power strip is not supported properly
issue_context.body:
**Home Assistant release with the issue:**
0.95

**Last working Home Assistant release (if known):**

None

**Operating environment (Hass.io/Docker/Windows/etc.):**

Doesn't matter.

**Component/platform:**
components/tplink


**Description of problem:**
The Kasa HS300 powerstrip is now supported by pyhs100, but is not added to home-assistant properly (only one plug will appear)

This is because pyhs100 derives the SmartStrip class from SmartPlug, which is what home-assistant checks for so home assistant believes it is simply a plug.  This is simple to fix, we add the child devices of the SmartStrip when it's a SmartStrip.

The following should fix it: dberlin/home-assistant@477f9ac411fad25641992ca67f9b7d2c253303f8

I'll test and create a pull request.

review_comments: Without looking into the details how the context is derived, is there a possibility that it is not definitely unique without involving the device id with it, too?

At least on the two HS107's I have to test with, the value for context that pyHS100 provides is `{deviceId}00` for Plug 1 and `{deviceId}01` for Plug 2, so I decided that would be unique enough to use for unique_id

Also, I debated using `mac` in the `if self.smartplug.context is None` case to retain current behavior, but opted for consistency, if you'd prefer defaulting to `mac`, I'm happy to make that change though.

Hmm, I'm not sure what is going to happen for those who have been using this integration when the id suddenly changes, but I wouldn't mind to keep using context here and fix the issue upstream. But in case the device id changes, is there a need to migrate them? Can someone from @home-assistant/core clarify what's the best approach?

This doesn't need to be a breaking change.  Without knowing about this change, I re-did a lot of this work (see doc change at https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant.io/pull/10382 and main PR at https://github.com/home-assistant/home-assistant/pull/26655 ).

To avoid breaking change, for SmartStrip Plug (and only for those plugs), give them a unique_id mac_address + "_" + devid (or append the plug number).  Non-smart-strip plugs can just use mac like before.

Note that I didn't notice that smartstrip builds a SmartPlug for each outlet (I was reverse engineering the sys_info and the network protocol and didn't even realize that the KP400 looks like a SmartStrip because I didn't know they made those).

Another FWIW: if you update this block (and remove the previous `self._alias` declaration) the individual outlets will use the names/aliases given to them in the Kasa app.

```python
                if self.smartplug.context is None:
                    self._device_id = self.smartplug.sys_info["deviceId"]
                    self._alias = self.smartplug.alias
                else:
                    self._device_id = self.smartplug.context
                    self._alias = [
                        child
                        for child in self.smartplug.sys_info["children"]
                        if child["id"] == self.smartplug.context
                    ][0]["alias"]
```
